advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Serialize/atomically write the comment_id_divergence.json debounce state (flock + atomic write) to match alert_store's concurrency handling.
evidence: invariants.py: `state_path.write_text(json.dumps({"consecutive": consecutive, "pass_id": pass_id}) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")` — no flock, no atomic temp+rename
alert_store.py:41-56 documents and applies `fcntl.LOCK_EX` for concurrent reconciler writers; alert_store._atomic_write uses fsutil.atomic_write to avoid truncated writes
The read (_read_comment_divergence_state) then write is a non-atomic RMW; a concurrent second pass can clobber the incremented counter, defeating the 2-consecutive-pass debounce
Shared resource: 'state_path = repo_root / "bridge_state" / _COMMENT_DIVERGENCE_STATE_FILE' (invariants.py:404) — a file under the shared bridge_state tree

Second executor: alert_store.append docstring 'Concurrent writers from multiple reconciler instances serialize on an advisory fcntl.LOCK_EX flock' (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/alert_store.py:41-44); binding_repository.py:190 'the file is shared with other writers'

WRITE (non-atomic, unguarded): 'state_path.write_text(json.dumps({"consecutive": consecutive, "pass_id": pass_id}) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")' (invariants.py:409-411) — truncate-then-write, no flock, no temp+replace

Sibling guard 2 (atomic write): '_atomic_write' -> 'fsutil.atomic_write(path, content, permissions=0o600, fsync=True)' with temp file + os.replace (alert_store.py:87-107); BindingRepository.save uses '_write_json_atomically' (binding_repository.py:279)

Harm: a concurrent instance's read_text observes a truncated/partial JSON write of the divergence-count file; the surrounding fail-open (invariants.py:372) silently resets consecutive to 0, so the debounce counter loses a divergent-pass observation and the N=2 alert can fail to fire when it should — the silent-inertness class (bug aa7b) this invariant exists to catch.
advisory.finding: The debounce state file bridge_state/comment_id_divergence.json is written with a plain, non-atomic, unlocked `state_path.write_text(...)`, whereas the sibling alert_store deliberately serializes concurrent reconciler writers with fcntl.LOCK_EX and uses atomic_write. Two reconciler instances persisting concurrently can interleave read-modify-write and corrupt or lose the consecutive-divergence counter.
merged_from: New writer of shared bridge_state/comment_id_divergence.json uses a non-atomic, unlocked read-modify-write, unlike every sibling accessor of the same bridge_state tree which serializes via fcntl.flock and writes atomically (temp+os.replace+fsync). A concurrent reconciler instance can read a torn/half-written state file (or lose the counter update), corrupting the cross-pass debounce counter.
scenarios: Two reconciler passes/instances run against the same repo_root concurrently and both fold+persist the divergence counter
A crash mid-write leaves a truncated file (caught fail-open, resetting to 0 and re-arming the debounce)

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify/adjust the divergence definition (or docstring) so it is explicit that UNKNOWN_COMMENT_ID sentinel recordings count as map growth and are treated as healthy.
evidence: binding_store.comment_ids_gained_this_pass: `len(self._data.get("comment_ids", {})) - self._comment_ids_at_load` — grows whenever record_comment_id adds any value, including the sentinel
dispatch_apply_phases.py:351 `recorder(key, comment_id or UNKNOWN_COMMENT_ID)` — records a sentinel entry (map grows) even when no truthful id was returned
invariants.py docstring frames this as reading the bug-aa7b signal ('nothing compared successful posts against map growth'), but sentinel recordings satisfy gained>0 and read as healthy
advisory.finding: The divergence predicate `divergent = posted > 0 and gained <= 0` treats any comment_ids map growth as healthy, but _record_comment_id records the UNKNOWN_COMMENT_ID sentinel (`recorder(key, comment_id or UNKNOWN_COMMENT_ID)`) which grows the map. A regression where posts succeed on a transport that never returns a real id (the aa7b class the docstring invokes) is therefore counted as healthy, so this invariant does NOT detect that specific class — it only detects posts where recording is entirely skipped (no key / no recorder).
scenarios: Cloud/ACLI transport posts comments and records UNKNOWN_COMMENT_ID for each — posted>0, gained>0, divergent=False, no alert even though no real comment id was ever captured

advisory.finding: The newly-added invariant call in reconcile._persist_and_log (its fail-open try/except wrapper) is not exercised by any test. The invariant function is thoroughly unit-tested in isolation, but the added wiring — that a divergent pass routed through _persist_and_log actually invokes check_comment_id_recording and that the try/except swallows an invariant-check exception without breaking sync — has no direct coverage.
